text:
oliver: Quick q — we need to nail down the eval sampling strategy for model onboarding. Current approach runs the full bench on every model; cost is exploding, and we still miss regressions from corner cases. looking for tradeoffs (catch rate vs $).

maya: +1 on cost. we should split checks into fast probes vs full runs. fast probes for surface-level perf/compat, full bench only for flagged models or periodic resamples.

raj: Agree. Two baseline ideas: stratified sampling by model family/size + change-triggered full bench (e.g., new quantization, arch change). That keeps coverage for high-risk classes.

carmen: We also need to keep backward-compat signals. A small targeted suite that historically catches regressions (hot prompts + token-level diffs) could run on every ingest — very cheap.

oliver: Sounds good. Can we sketch thresholds? e.g., if fast probe latency or perplexity delta > X -> full bench. If model is within top-10% by size -> auto full bench?

maya: Proposal: fast_probe (30s): smoke latency pkts, run 50 example prompts, check for mem growth and basic correctness heuristics. If any metric trips -> full_bench queue. Thresholds: latency +20% or token-error > 5%.

raj: +1 but prefer absolute thresholds for latency (e.g., >200ms for 1k-context) instead of % to avoid noise from tiny models. For quality, use pass/fail on curated assertion set (not raw perplexity).

carmen: On sampling policy: stratify by (model_family, param_bucket, quantization). Maintain an LRU-ish sampled set where we always include at least one model from each bucket every 48h. Then do random draws within bucket for extra coverage.

oliver: Nice. How about cost controls: budget cap per day for full benches, with priority rules (new onboards > weekly resamples > edge picks). If cap reached, defer low-priority resamples.

maya: We should also make gate decisions auditable: log which probes tripped + diff snapshots. Add a compact event format: {model_id, probe_id, metric, observed, threshold, action}.

carmen: Example event JSON (for ops):
```
{
  "model_id": "m-abc123",
  "probe": "smoke-latency-1k",
  "metric": "p95_ms",
  "observed": "312",
  "threshold": "200",
  "action": "enqueue_full_bench"
}
```

raj: For sampling frequency: heavy families (e.g., LLaMA-like forks) -> sample every 24h. medium -> 72h. small -> weekly. Tunables via config.

oliver: What about changes that should always trigger full bench? e.g., quantization bitwidth change, tokenizer updates, new compilation kernels.

maya: Those are high-risk — treat them as "policy triggers" that immediately enqueue. Also if customer-facing flagged model (private deployment) -> mandatory full bench.

carmen: On tooling: add a lightweight dashboard to show sample coverage per bucket, budget burn rate, queued benches, and last-fail diffs. Ops needs quick rerun button.

raj: QA: keep a small always-on regression set (100 prompts) that historical data shows catches 95% of visible regressions. This runs as the cheap probe. The full bench remains our ground truth.

oliver: Followups: 1) define the cheap probe suite (maya + qa) 2) implement bucket stratifier + policy config (carmen) 3) budget enforcement + priority queue (infra) 4) audit event schema + dashboard (raj). Anyone object?

maya: I'll draft the probe suite and thresholds by EOD tomorrow.

carmen: I'll start the stratifier shim and a PoC sampling job.

raj: I'll spec the audit schema + runbook for triage.

infra-bot: Scheduled job created: sampling-prototype (owner: carmen) — runs hourly on staging. See /ops/jobs/2143056789-sampling-prototype.

qa-bot: Small regression set results (last 24h): 0 fails on staging; p95 latency medians: 180ms. Will push list to #eng-ml-archives.

oliver: Cool, thanks. Let's reconvene after the PoC. If we can shave cost by 40% while keeping regression catch high, that's a win. :+1:
